content.title: About
content.content: A hash brown is a fried patty of shredded potato, commonly served in school cafeterias as part of a hot lunch. Potato is one of the world’s most widely cultivated vegetables, rich in carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hash browns originated in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became a staple in school menus because they are easy to prepare.
Potatoes are about 70% water and contain roughly 17% starch, making them an excellent source of energy.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties, but starchy types are usually chosen for hash browns.
In some countries hash browns are served with cheese, bacon, or sour cream.
Potatoes were first domesticated in the Andes more than 7,000 years ago.

items.title: Source of Vitamin C
items.content: Potatoes provide a substantial portion of the daily vitamin C requirement, which supports immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Rich in Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Contains Vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Provides Dietary Fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Energy Source
items.content: The starch in potatoes is quickly converted to glucose, delivering rapid energy—important for school‑age children.

items.title: High Fat Content When Fried
items.content: Hash browns are cooked in oil, which can make them calorie‑dense and high in saturated fat.

items.title: Added Salt
items.content: Salt is often used for flavor, which may be a concern for those monitoring sodium intake.

items.title: Rare Potato Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Acrylamide Formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound; avoid over‑cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hash browns are served hot, usually as a few patties. They can be eaten on their own or paired with salads, sauces, cottage cheese, or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked hash browns keep in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days in an airtight container. Reheat in an oven or skillet to restore a crispy exterior.
